question: Locate the anchor function for the state_code field in the console.log object whose action is account.submit after filling the email field, filling the one-time code, checking Remember this device, and clicking Submit on the page. The anchor function is the first target-specific state encoding value constructor on the dynamic behavior chain: after routing, delegated click capture, form-state collection and input preparation, its function body itself constructs the target observable state_code value rather than merely collecting inputs, dispatching control, wrapping a return value, or writing to the console. Return exactly one complete function as a single JSON object (see answer_format). Do not return generic utilities, event handlers, the full call chain, or the final sink. Note: you may only inspect code under captures; the full codebase is not accessible.
anchor_definition_general: General rule for resolving ambiguity: a function is target-specific with respect to the observable described above if at least one statement in its body either constructs/binds the target value, writes the target field, or dispatches the target action — and removing that statement would break the observed target output under the prescribed interaction. A function is generic if it is a reusable utility (hash/encode/serialize/normalize/collect-features), a control-flow dispatcher (router/interceptor-pipeline/event-bus/scheduler), or a preparation routine (validate input/collect UI state/lifecycle hook) whose body would look the same regardless of which behavior it currently serves. The anchor is the unique target-specific function on the chain whose immediate caller is generic — equivalently, the shallowest target-specific function on the path from the trigger to the sink. Three situations commonly cause confusion: (1) If a target-specific function C is called by a generic dispatcher B and itself calls a generic utility D, the anchor is C, not B and not D. (2) If a generic function A merely writes whatever its callee B returns into the target field, and B computes that value, the anchor is B. (3) If the target-specific statement is one branch inside a larger function F, F remains a valid anchor candidate.
anchor_worked_example: Worked example (different scenario, for illustration only): A checkout page emits body.order_sig_v2 after Submit Order. Chain: click Submit -> construct order draft (generic prep) -> encode checkout state (generic prep) -> collect async profile receipt (generic prep) -> compose request envelope (generic prep) -> run interceptor pipeline (generic dispatcher) -> select sealing interceptor (ANCHOR) -> canonicalize payload fields (nested helper) -> fold payload with receipt + pepper (nested helper) -> compute digest (core utility) -> write body.order_sig_v2 -> send request (wrapper/sink). The sealing interceptor is the anchor because its caller is generic and its body explains why order_sig_v2 is produced. Apply the same reasoning to the actual page and bundle below.

function_name.description: The identifier on the function declaration line in the captured bundle slice (the name immediately after the `function` keyword). Use the name as it appears in captures, not a guessed source-level name.

file.description: Path to the JavaScript file under captures/ that contains the function. Must match visible_corpus.

slice.description: One contiguous source slice covering exactly one complete function body in the captured bundle.

start_line.description: 1-based inclusive start line of the function in file.

end_line.description: 1-based inclusive end line of the function in file.

start_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice begins.

end_offset.description: 0-based byte offset in file where the function slice ends (exclusive).

code.description: Exact source text of the complete function from start_offset to end_offset. Must start with `function <function_name>(` and end with the closing brace of that function.

public_constraints: Only code visible under captures is in scope.
Submit exactly one JSON object matching answer_format.response_schema; do not wrap it in markdown fences unless the evaluation harness explicitly requires that.

The target value is a stable 12-character state code and should not be confused with account.prepare/account.audit decoys or other state_code-like fields under non-target actions.
